reason: The flower opens, but only partly. Negating open (PATO_0000610) would wrongly say the flower is closed, and no term exists for 'opens only partly'.

target: new: conjunction of two qualities of one bearer (orbicular PATO_0001934 + asymmetrical PATO_0000616)
reason: This is an orbicular outline that is unequal on its two sides. It is two existing qualities of one part, so no new term is needed. The 'obliquely truncate' class (FLOPO:0991383) should not be copied for every shape.
Lateral veins that run obliquely are slanted, neither perpendicular nor parallel to the midrib. That is the definition of PATO_0002481.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum / hyphenated compound of two values)
reason: This is a compound of two shape values: ovate (PATO_0001891), and heart shaped (PATO_0000948) taken as an approximate value. It is handled like 'linear-lanceolate', not by a new term.

Corolla lobes that overlap to the left are a contort aestivation, which falls under imbricate (overlapping) in the broad sense. The direction of the overlap is lost, but 4 statements do not justify a sinistrorse class.
Cymes arranged in a panicle form a thyrse: an indeterminate main axis with cymose lateral branches, which is the definition of FLOPO:0991199.
The leaf bears spines. 'Pectinately' says only that they are closely set like the teeth of a comb, which can be added as pectinate (FLOPO:0991033) when the source is annotated with two values.
The definition of urceolate is 'shaped like an urn or pitcher'.
Bark that splits into rectangular blocks is tessellated bark: structural elements arranged in quadrilateral units. The broader alternative is fissured (FLOPO:0991022).

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum / hyphenated compound of two values)
reason: This is a compound of two margin values that both have terms: repand (FLOPO:0991186) and serrated (PATO_0001206).
The dots are resin glands on the surface. That is the definition of gland-dotted, which has 'glandular-punctate' as a synonym.
Moss leaf cells that are rhombic with rounded corners. The shape is rhomboid; the rounded corners are a minor modifier.
Shallow pinnate lobing is pinnately lobed, as opposed to the deeper pinnatifid (FLOPO:0991078).
A petiole, bract or leaf base that forms a sheath round the axis is sheathing.
A shallow cut at an apex, base or margin is a notch. Cut (PATO_0001978, synonym 'incised') is defined by deep incisions and would overstate it.
Leaves or scales that are widely separated from their neighbours are distant (synonym remote). The example texts are garbled, but this reading is clear.
A stick-like stigma or trunk is rod-shaped, and rod-like and rod-shaped are synonyms of cylindrical.

The word could mean straw-coloured, which is straw yellow (PATO_0104343, synonym 'straw'), or a dry, stiff texture like straw. The two examples cannot settle which, so a rule could be wrong either way.
'Sub-' marks an approximate value of 'pinnately divided', which is pinnatisect (cut to the midrib into segments on either side). Pattern 01 handles it, so no term is needed.

target: docs/annotation-context-patterns.md (continuum / hyphenated compound of two values)
reason: This is a compound of two shape values: square (PATO_0000413), taken as an approximate value, and obovate (PATO_0001936).

Secondary veins that end at the marginal teeth are craspedodromous, defined as 'secondary branches terminating at the margin'. Like the other venation qualities, it inheres in the leaf's venation, not in a single vein.
Triqueter is the Latin form of triquetrous, which is already a related synonym of trigonous.
It is unclear whether this means a truncate base that also bears a spur or a spur that is truncate. With only 4 statements, the words without context do not give a reliable quality.
Moss leaf cells whose walls are unevenly thickened. The quality belongs to the cell wall, so the rule should place it on the wall of the cell.
This describes the dry habitat a plant lives in or is adapted to, not its form or position. Saxicolous was kept because it says where the plant grows; xeric does not.
'Broadly' only qualifies the proportions of an urceolate shape, as with 'broadly ovate'.
A bulb tunic or neck made of tough threads is fibrous. 'fiber-l ike' in the source is a transcription split of the same word.
A once-geniculate awn is bent like a knee, following the earlier rule geniculate → bent. That the awn bends once, not twice, is lost.
A chasmophyte grows in rock crevices, and saxicolous is defined as growing on rocks or in rock crevices.

'Stipular spines deficient' states that the part it modifies is absent, so pattern 15 applies to that part. The Latin 'demum deficientes' ('finally lacking') describes parts that fall later, which is a stage and should go to review.
